svg.aria-label: Perfboard layout on a 14 by 20 hole board, seen from the front
svg.text: Perfboard layout, seen from the front (the ring side)
A stock 40 × 60 mm board with 14 × 20 holes, its bottom border cut off, drawn to scale. Dashed outlines are parts on the back.
Button 1, the ring and the resistors are on the front, and so are all the wires. Purple dashed parts are off the board, with their leads drawn to the holes they solder to.
LiPo battery, behind the board (53 × 34 × 10 mm)
LED ring pads on its back, about every 90° (order to check)
XIAO ESP32-C3, on the back, chip and USB-C facing away from the board
back, standing, flat face toward the XIAO
back, standing, flat face toward the XIAO
Wires on the board (insulated, all on the front)
Wire A, 6, 18 to 6, 9: D2 to button 1, under the ring
Wire B, 14, 17 to 10, 6: ground to button 1, under the ring
Wire C, 10, 5 to 1, 12: ground from button 1 to the left side, under the ring
Wire D, 10, 15 to 2, 15: R1 to Q1 base, below the ring
Jumper E, 10, 16 to 13, 15: R3 to Q2 base
Jumper F, 2, 14 to 2, 20: ground down to button 2 and R7
Solid lines are solder bridges or bare links on the front; black is ground, red is 3V3. Gold squares are pins and legs of parts on the back.
Pink dotted circles: where the ring sits. No part or bare link goes under it; only insulated wires.
Off the board (purple): the LED ring, the motor, the 1000 µF capacitor, the battery and the antenna. Ring pad positions and order are approximate.
The battery's two leads solder to the BAT+ and BAT− pads on the XIAO's underside, near its middle; go by the labels printed there. Hole 8 takes a sense wire from BAT+.
